decisions.reason: The champagne-gold study must preserve the established architectural quality, but it does not change any Hero V geometry or construction rule.
The source confirms the letterforms read as a unified family but introduces only a material-treatment direction; the E and L construction requirements remain unchanged.
The source praises the optical drawing result but does not alter the second V's optical construction, design DNA, or right-arm treatment.
Investigating champagne-gold color and finish does not change the selected kerning, spacing rhythm, or pair-spacing reference.
The material-treatment decision does not modify the É accent's literal geometric derivation from the Hero V.
The champagne-gold direction leaves the established second-V height hierarchy unchanged.
The instruction to retain timeless architectural quality is compatible with the existing preservation policy but does not add, remove, or redefine any locked asset.
Color and material treatment do not change the all-caps wordmark selection.
The source does not change the required peak alignment between the Hero V and É accent.
The champagne-gold finish investigation does not alter the shared-baseline requirement.
The source requests interpretation of a material reference but does not necessarily change the existing comparison-proof format or its review dimensions.
The material-treatment decision has no effect on the accepted formats for accessible review images.
